sources.entry: awesome-ralph by Martin Joly - A curated list of resources about Ralph, the AI coding technique that runs AI coding agents in automated loops until specifications are fulfilled.

summary.one_liner: A curated link list of resources about Ralph (Ralph Wiggum), Geoffrey Huntley's technique of running AI coding agents in automated loops until a spec is complete.
summary.what_it_does: This is an "awesome" list, not a software project: it collects links to articles, playbooks, tutorials, videos, podcasts, community threads and third-party Ralph implementations. It opens with the core idea, a bash loop that repeatedly feeds a prompt file to an AI coding agent, and lists principles such as fresh context per iteration, progress kept in files and git history, and backpressure from tests and lints. The sections are Official Resources, Playbooks & Methodology, Implementations (Claude Code plugins, standalone, tool-specific, multi-agent), Tutorials, Articles, Videos & Podcasts, Community, Related Tools and Support. Each entry has a one-line description, and the implementations section names projects for specific agents such as Cursor, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot and Goose.
use_cases: Finding Ralph Wiggum loop implementations for Claude Code
Learning the Ralph technique from primary sources
Browsing tutorials on autonomous AI coding loops
Finding Ralph tools for Cursor, OpenCode, Copilot or Goose
Locating Ralph community discussions and videos
notable: Curated index of Ralph implementations grouped by type (plugins, standalone, tool-specific, multi-agent)
Includes the playbook file-structure pattern (PROMPT_plan.md, PROMPT_build.md, loop.sh, IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md)
Links to primary sources from Geoffrey Huntley, the technique's creator
Lists community forums including a subreddit and a Discord
caveats: Link list only; the linked projects and articles are not reviewed or verified here
Some linked implementations are tied to specific agents (Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, Copilot, Goose)
